title: Northeast Blackout 2003: EMS alarm failure, silent situational-awareness loss, and control-room/IT split
summary: The 2003 blackout is encoded here only at one grain: the software/control-room visibility failure in FirstEnergy’s EMS. The record preserves the Task Force account that the alarm process and related EMS functions failed silently enough that operators did not understand their visibility had collapsed while the grid degraded.

claims.claim: The U.S.-Canada Task Force final report identifies FE computer failures on August 14, 2003, including lost alarm functionality, lost remote-console functionality, and disrupted primary/backup server support from early afternoon through the blackout sequence.
what_would_change_status: A later official investigation changes the EMS/alarm chronology or system role.

claims.claim: The report records primary/backup alarm-server failure and slowed screen refresh, and says IT staff did not notify or confirm with the control room before/after reboot attempts; from 14:14 until at least 15:42 operators did not understand the extent of lost systems and took no actions to restore reliable state.

sequence_of_events.event: EMS/alarm functionality degraded and alarm processing stalled.
The EMS did not effectively alert operators to its own alarm failure.
IT support activity did not become shared operational awareness in the control room.
Operators lacked situational awareness as transmission lines and contingency conditions deteriorated.
